items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: I was in Little Rock with a bunch of the jazz musicians at that time, so I wasn't there that night, but I remember quite well when that happened.

ctx.x: Thank you very much, sir. Today's subject, jazz, Dixieland, whatever you want to call it, by one of the greats, Mr. Johnny Wiggins, Wiggs, I beg your pardon, sir, and by one of the true authorities in the country from Tulane University, Mr. Dick Allen. High Karate After Shave and Cologne presents Electric Train! Back in tune with more of Let's Talk It Over, we're going to get back in just a moment to Snoozer Quinn on My Melancholy Baby, and we'll have some comments on that by Mr. Johnny Wiggs of Johnny Wiggs and…
Yeah, I couldn't think of his last name, but I have thought of it. Tell him, Dick. Papa John Joseph.

It's Joe. Oh, this is Joe Sean. This is a record shop on. Oh, yes, uh-huh. Yeah, well, they could find his records. The shoppers were all there. They could find many, many jazz records there. Uh-huh. That's one of the places in town. Now, do you recall the time when Papa John Joseph played for the, uh, when John's son, uh, prisonership? And he played there, and he gave, uh, President Johnson one of, uh, gave President Johnson's daughter one of his records. Uh, well, I wasn't invited to that. I miss a lot of…
